162.nameOrigin: Retained geographic working name; a prehistoric native name is not known.

163.name: Xiaohe
163.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label for early Bronze Age Tarim remains; adapted to this game region.

164.name: Majiayao
164.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label for a prehistoric northwestern Chinese culture; adapted to this game region.

165.name: Hongshan
165.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label for a prehistoric northeastern Chinese culture; adapted to this game region.

166.name: Anzan
166.nameOrigin: Elamite form of Anshan, an ancient southern Iranian city and region; game boundaries are adapted.

167.name: Meluhha
167.nameOrigin: Bronze Age Mesopotamian name generally associated with the Indus civilization; its own self-name is unknown.

168.name: Kuru
168.nameOrigin: Later ancient kingdom name, adopted for this game region; not a verified prehistoric self-name.

169.name: Kunlun
169.nameOrigin: Name from Chinese mythical mountain geography, adapted to this fantasy plateau; not a historical name for all Tibet.

170.name: Baodun
170.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label for prehistoric Chengdu Plain settlements; adapted to this game region.

171.name: Liangzhu
171.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label for a prehistoric lower Yangtze culture; adapted to this game region.

173.name: Meluhha Coast
173.nameOrigin: Game subdivision of the wider Indus world, not a separately attested ancient place-name.

174.name: Dakshinapatha
174.nameOrigin: Later ancient southern-region name, adapted to this game map; not a recovered prehistoric self-name.

175.name: Vanga
175.nameOrigin: Later ancient regional name, adopted for this game chart.

176.name: Suvarnabhumi
176.nameOrigin: Name from later tradition whose historical location is uncertain; placement here is a game interpretation.

177.name: Shixia
177.nameOrigin: Modern archaeological label associated with prehistoric Guangdong; adapted to this game region.

181.name: Samudra

mononofu169.note: Mononofu is an old Japanese word for a warrior. The earlier form mononopu appears in the Man’yōshū, where it also refers to people serving the court.

regionalCast156.name: Honeywife
regionalCast156.line: There was a little pin in the rushes. No bigger than a bee. I’ve kept it in my apron in case his mother comes.

regionalCast156.name: Kennel Girl
regionalCast156.line: She eats enough for two dogs now. Watch where she goes when she carries her supper away.

regionalCast156.name: Brindled hound
regionalCast156.line: The hound puts one paw on a crust. She looks back at the reeds before picking it up.

regionalCast156.name: Honey jar
regionalCast156.line: The rim is sticky. One little brown dog hair has caught in the wax.

regionalCast156.name: Slingmaker
regionalCast156.line: That lifting rope is mine. My son knows how to let it run without taking the skin off his palms. I wish I knew which shift they put him on.

regionalCast156.name: Sounder of Tingis
regionalCast156.line: They paid me to count the barrows. Three loads went to the harbour. None went on my slate as stone.

regionalCast156.name: Harbour surveyor
regionalCast156.line: I paid for three loads. The men keep asking where the hill went. A hill is a quantity of earth, surely?

regionalCast156.name: Harbour lifting rope
regionalCast156.line: The outer turn is pale where a sling has drawn tight around a heavy load.

regionalCast156.name: Shore Netmaker
regionalCast156.line: A net is good for hauling somebody aboard. A man with pitch on his hands has been mending mine.

regionalCast156.name: Phocaean Caulker
regionalCast156.line: I can hear where a hull leaks. Getting the people on this shore to lend me a boat is the harder part.

regionalCast156.name: Petta’s cousin
regionalCast156.line: She has chosen her dress. She has chosen her guest. Everyone here seems to think there is still a decision to make.

regionalCast156.name: Net drying rack
regionalCast156.line: One corner is mended with a sailor’s knot. The rest is tied the way the fishers on this shore do it.

regionalCast156.name: Grain Widow
regionalCast156.line: I can tell seed grain by touch in the dark. Last winter that was how I kept the levy from eating next year’s bread.

regionalCast156.name: Young Standard Bearer
regionalCast156.line: My mother says count the sacks yourself. My captain says trust the tally. They both put me on the same door.

regionalCast156.name: Winter Quartermaster
regionalCast156.line: Three barns. Two keys on this ring. I would give a great deal to know whose belt the third hangs from.

regionalCast156.name: Seed tally
regionalCast156.line: A deep cut marks each full cart. Three smaller cuts beside it mark the families who filled it.

regionalCast156.name: Myrto
regionalCast156.line: Try the threshing song. I can take the low part. I keep starting at the wrong place when I sing it alone.

regionalCast156.name: Iambe
regionalCast156.line: Take this stool to the well. If our guest wants quiet, I know a dozen excellent things I can keep to myself.

regionalCast156.name: Harvest sheaf
regionalCast156.line: Two loops of thread bind the last sheaf. One is knotted for a right hand, one for a left.

regionalCast156.name: Veia
regionalCast156.line: An onion for the pot? Pick it up first. An honest weight feels different in your hand once you know it.

regionalCast156.name: Larce
regionalCast156.line: People remember very precisely what they wish someone had said. Wet clay gives them time to reconsider.

regionalCast156.name: Keeper of Measures
regionalCast156.line: Ask who owns a field and you’ll get one answer at the gate and another at the far corner.

regionalCast156.name: Veia’s market balance
regionalCast156.line: The bronze pans hang almost level. The smaller weight bears a nick under its rim.

regionalCast156.name: Min Boatwoman
regionalCast156.line: See that empty boat? Whoever tied it knew the river. Whoever dressed it for a wedding had never set foot in it.

regionalCast156.name: Salt Clerk
regionalCast156.line: Every household pays at this crossing. I have two names here in a different hand.

regionalCast156.name: Dike Cutter
regionalCast156.line: Stand on the bank you mean to flood before you put a spade in the other one.

regionalCast156.name: White river sash
regionalCast156.line: Two turns of pale cloth hang from the mooring post, high enough to show above muddy water.

regionalCast156.name: Potter’s Daughter
regionalCast156.line: Put both hands under the jar. I heard a voice when the water ran out between my fingers.

regionalCast156.name: Rope Twister
regionalCast156.line: Take the wet end. That splice will draw tight. If it slips now, I want to know on land.

regionalCast156.name: Reed Pilot
regionalCast156.line: Twice on the pole for a shelf. Once for deep water. You’ll hear the difference when you need both hands on a line.

regionalCast156.name: Potter’s fish jar
regionalCast156.line: Something the length of your little finger turns beneath the water.

regionalCast156.name: Keeper of the Gold
regionalCast156.line: I have watched that fire every night of the feast. Today I woke with my cloak drawn up around my shoulders. Who did that?

regionalCast156.name: Watcher’s Foster Son
regionalCast156.line: Take the short circuit and our herd will have enough for years. She keeps looking past it toward the common wells.

regionalCast156.name: Remount Keeper
regionalCast156.line: Find where the white mare drinks when nobody leads her. That’s the crossing I’d trust.

regionalCast156.name: Looped bridle
regionalCast156.line: The leather is polished where a rider changes horses without setting a foot on the ground.

regionalCast156.name: Axle Maker
regionalCast156.line: Listen to the left wheel. Two creaks and a pause. I’d like it back in my yard before there’s a third.

regionalCast156.name: Marsh Ferrier
regionalCast156.line: Two heifers and the wagon. Anyone wanting passage with them can come take a turn at my sounding pole.

regionalCast156.name: Young Iron Warden
regionalCast156.line: Two companies have sworn to put away their weapons. Both captains say I’m to give the first key to them.

regionalCast156.name: Spare wagon wheel
regionalCast156.line: One spoke is younger and paler than the rest. Someone has tested it under load.

regionalCast156.name: Notch Cutter
regionalCast156.line: Somebody has brought back my oar. I cut that notch for a girl who could barely reach the thole.

regionalCast156.name: Fjord Sounder
regionalCast156.line: I know our boat by the noise of the oar in the socket. That noise out there this morning was my brother rowing a stranger’s boat.

regionalCast156.name: Mended shore oar
regionalCast156.line: A pale binding covers an older repair. The marks near the grip face the rower.
